146		return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
147			token, ok := strings.CutPrefix(r.Header.Get("Authorization"), "Bearer ")
148			if !ok {
149				writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "unauthorized", "send an API key as Authorization: Bearer <token>")
150				return
151			}
152			key, ok := s.store.APIKeyByToken(strings.TrimSpace(token))
153			if !ok || key.RevokedAt != nil {
154				writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "unauthorized", "unknown or revoked API key")
155				return
156			}
157			m, ok := s.store.Member(key.OrgID, key.UserID)
158			if !ok {

160				return
161			}

163			p := auth.Principal{OrgID: key.OrgID, UserID: key.UserID, KeyID: key.ID, Role: m.Role}
164			if r.Method != http.MethodGet && !auth.CanWrite(p.Role) {
165				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "forbidden", "viewers can only read")
166				return

// CustomerImportRow is one record of a customer import: its values, and the line of the file where it starts.

// RowError is a row of an import that is refused, and why.
type RowError struct {
	Row  int    `json:"row"`
	Code string `json:"error"`
}

// The reasons an import refuses a row. A row gets the first of these that applies, in this order.
const (
	RowMissingName          = "missing_name"
	RowInvalidEmail         = "invalid_email"
	RowInvalidPaymentMethod = "invalid_payment_method"
	RowEmailTaken           = "email_taken"
	RowDuplicateEmail       = "duplicate_email"
)

// ImportCustomers creates a customer for each row, in order, or none at all. Every row is checked as CreateCustomer

// is refused, nothing is created and the refused rows are returned in order. With dryRun, the rows are checked and nothing
// is created. Otherwise the created customers are returned.
func (s *Store) ImportCustomers(orgID string, rows []CustomerImportRow, now time.Time, dryRun bool) ([]Customer, []RowError, error) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	if _, ok := s.orgs[orgID]; !ok {
		return nil, nil, ErrNotFound
	}
	var refused []RowError
	seen := map[string]bool{}
	prepared := make([]Customer, 0, len(rows))
	for _, row := range rows {
		name, email, pm := strings.TrimSpace(row.Name), strings.TrimSpace(row.Email), strings.TrimSpace(row.DefaultPaymentMethod)
		key := normEmail(email)
		id, exists := s.customersByEmail[key]
		code := ""
		switch {
		case name == "":

		case !validEmail(email):
			code = RowInvalidEmail
		case pm != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(pm, "pm_"):
			code = RowInvalidPaymentMethod
		case exists && s.customers[id].OrgID == orgID:
			code = RowEmailTaken
		case seen[key]:
			code = RowDuplicateEmail
		}
		if validEmail(email) {
			seen[key] = true
		}
		if code != "" {
			refused = append(refused, RowError{Row: row.Line, Code: code})
			continue
		}
		prepared = append(prepared, Customer{OrgID: orgID, Name: name, Email: email, DefaultPaymentMethod: pm,
			Metadata: row.Metadata, CreatedAt: now.UTC()})
	}
	if len(refused) > 0 || dryRun {
		return nil, refused, nil
	}
	out := make([]Customer, 0, len(prepared))
	for _, c := range prepared {
		c.ID = s.newID("cus")
		s.customers[c.ID] = c
		s.customersByEmail[normEmail(c.Email)] = c.ID
		out = append(out, copyCustomer(c))
	}
	return out, nil, nil
}

// Customer returns one of an organization's customers.
func (s *Store) Customer(orgID, id string) (Customer, bool) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	c, ok := s.customers[id]
	if !ok || c.OrgID != orgID {
		return Customer{}, false
	}
	return copyCustomer(c), true
}

// CustomerByID returns a customer of any organization (background jobs and the admin tool).
func (s *Store) CustomerByID(id string) (Customer, bool) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	c, ok := s.customers[id]
	return copyCustomer(c), ok
}

// Customers returns an organization's customers, oldest first.
func (s *Store) Customers(orgID string) []Customer {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	out := []Customer{}
	for _, c := range s.customers {
		if c.OrgID == orgID {
			out = append(out, copyCustomer(c))
		}
	}
	sortCustomers(out)
	return out
}
